items.title: degrade_episodic: sqlite3.OperationalError: no such savepoint: degrade_row (26x/7d in Hermes session-end sleep)

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: needs-reproduction
labels.description: Reported behavior needs a minimal reproduction on a supported current path.

items.body:
## Summary

`degrade_episodic` in `mnemosyne/core/beam.py` repeatedly fails with `sqlite3.OperationalError: no such savepoint: degrade_row`, twice per incident (the `RELEASE` at ~line 8018, then the `ROLLBACK TO` at ~line 8022 inside the exception handler).

Observed in production: Hermes Agent embeds `mnemosyne-memory 3.15.1` (installed under `/usr/local/lib/hermes-agent/venv`). Across 7 days of agent logs there are **26 distinct traceback chains**, all during session-end sleep consolidation. After the failure the run continues via the outer handler, but the row's tier state is not tracked in `results["tier1_to_tier2"]`, and the second exception is logged with a copy-pasted message from a different handler:

```
INFO mnemosyne.core.beam: Regex extraction failed, skipping
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../mnemosyne/core/beam.py", line 8018, in degrade_episodic
    cursor.execute("RELEASE degrade_row")
sqlite3.OperationalError: no such savepoint: degrade_row

During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../mnemosyne/core/beam.py", line 8022, in degrade_episodic
    cursor.execute("ROLLBACK TO degrade_row")
sqlite3.OperationalError: no such savepoint: degrade_row
```

The `Regex extraction failed, skipping` message is wrong for this code path — it belongs to a different handler and makes log triage misleading.

## Analysis

Per-row flow is:

```python
cursor.execute("SAVEPOINT degrade_row")
try:
    ...UPDATE + _refresh_episodic_embedding(row["id"], ...)
    cursor.execute("RELEASE degrade_row")
except Exception:
    try:
        cursor.execute("ROLLBACK TO degrade_row")
        cursor.execute("RELEASE degrade_row")
    except Exception:
        logger.info("Regex extraction failed, skipping", exc_info=True)
```

A savepoint disappears when the enclosing transaction is committed or rolled back. Likely causes:

1. Something on the same connection commits/rolls back between `SAVEPOINT` and `RELEASE` — e.g. a helper called inside the block (`_refresh_episodic_embedding`) or a nested `local_llm` callback issuing `COMMIT`/implicit transaction end.
2. Reentrancy: if `degrade_episodic` can run concurrently/nested (multiple sessions ending sleep at once), a second `RELEASE degrade_row` from the inner call destroys the name for the outer call. A per-call unique savepoint name (e.g. `degrade_row_{row_id}`) would rule this class out.

When the RELEASE fails **after** the UPDATE succeeded, the degradation work may actually be committed while `results` counts it as failed (or vice versa after a rollback) — the drift this savepoint exists to prevent (added for C18.b) can still slip through in this path.

## Suggested fix

- Use a unique savepoint name per row/call.
- Only `ROLLBACK TO`/`RELEASE` when the savepoint is known to still exist (track a flag; clear it right after a successful `RELEASE`).
- Audit helpers invoked inside the savepoint for hidden `COMMIT`s on the shared connection.
- Fix the copy-pasted log message to describe the actual event.

## Environment

- `mnemosyne-memory` 3.15.1 (installed as Hermes Agent dependency)
- Python 3.11.15, Linux x86_64, SQLite via stdlib `sqlite3`
- Trigger: sleep-time `degrade_episodic` during session-end consolidation, ~4 incidents/day

items.title: [Bug]: SessionDB open raises 'no such savepoint: fts_align_empty' on an unused pre-v3 home (empty messages + misaligned FTS source)

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
## Environment

- Hermes Agent `v0.21.4 (2026.9.21)`, commit `16fe260aab45a524df94c8f635352fd9e6e66fe5` (`main` at time of writing)
- Python 3.11.15, SQLite 3.53.1 (FTS5 present)
- Linux (Ubuntu), install kind: git

## Symptom

Opening a `SessionDB` whose `messages` table is **empty** and whose `messages_fts` is still
**pre-v3 (external-content over the raw `messages` table)** raises on open:

```
sqlite3.OperationalError: no such savepoint: fts_align_empty
```

User-visible form (this is how it was first observed, on two named profiles that had never been
used — `0` messages, `fts_storage_version = 1`):

```
⚠ Session store unavailable — this conversation will NOT be saved and cannot be
  resumed later. Searching past sessions is also disabled.
  Reason: the session database could not be opened.
  Details: no such savepoint: fts_align_empty
```

The trigger condition is exactly *"an unused home/profile created by a build older than
`FTS_STORAGE_VERSION 3`"* — the normal state of any profile you create and don't immediately
use. It is **not** specific to one machine; I reproduced it on-demand in a temp dir (below).

## Minimal reproduction

Self-contained; creates its own temp DB, touches no user data. Against current `main`:

```python
import sqlite3, sys, tempfile
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, "<repo-root>")
from hermes_state import SessionDB
from hermes_state_common import FTS_STORAGE_VERSION

tmp = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="fts-repro-"))
db_path = tmp / "state.db"

# 1. Build a DB at the current schema, then close it.
db = SessionDB(db_path=db_path)
assert db._fts_enabled, "needs FTS5"
db.close()

# 2. Downgrade to the pre-v3 shape: external-content FTS over raw `messages`
#    (no `messages_fts_src`), no rows, fts_storage_version = 1.
conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path)
v3_ddl = conn.execute("SELECT sql FROM sqlite_master WHERE name='messages_fts'").fetchone()[0]
legacy_ddl = v3_ddl.replace("'messages_fts_src'", "'messages'")
for t in ("messages_fts_insert", "messages_fts_delete", "messages_fts_update"):
    conn.execute(f"DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS {t}")
conn.execute("DROP TABLE IF EXISTS messages_fts")
conn.execute("DROP VIEW IF EXISTS messages_fts_src")
conn.execute(legacy_ddl)
conn.execute("DELETE FROM messages")
conn.execute("INSERT INTO state_meta(key,value) VALUES('fts_storage_version','1') "
             "ON CONFLICT(key) DO UPDATE SET value='1'")
conn.commit(); conn.close()

# 3. Reopen with current code -> raises.
SessionDB(db_path=db_path)   # sqlite3.OperationalError: no such savepoint: fts_align_empty
```

Observed traceback tail (unmodified current `main`):

```
  File ".../hermes_state.py", line 787, in _connect_and_init
    self._init_schema()
  File ".../hermes_state_schema.py", line 996, in _init_schema
    self._init_fts(cursor)
  File ".../hermes_state_schema.py", line 1174, in _init_fts
    self._migrate_misaligned_fts_source(cursor, legacy=legacy_fts)
  File ".../hermes_state_schema.py", line 376, in _migrate_misaligned_fts_source
    cursor.execute("ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT fts_align_empty")
sqlite3.OperationalError: no such savepoint: fts_align_empty
```

## Root cause (line-level)

The `not has_messages` branch of `_migrate_misaligned_fts_source` assumes the work it wraps in a
savepoint is transactional (`hermes_state_schema.py:369-379`):

```python
if not has_messages:
    cursor.execute("SAVEPOINT fts_align_empty")      # :371
    try:
        do_align()                                    # :373
        cursor.execute("RELEASE SAVEPOINT fts_align_empty")   # :374  <-- fails here
    except BaseException:
        cursor.execute("ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT fts_align_empty")  # :376  <-- fails again
        cursor.execute("RELEASE SAVEPOINT fts_align_empty")
        raise
```

`do_align()` calls `self._ensure_fts_schema(cursor, "messages_fts", FTS_SQL)`
(`hermes_state_schema.py:362`), which lives in `hermes_state_fts.py:327` and at **line 333** runs:

```python
cursor.executescript(ddl)
```

`sqlite3.Cursor.executescript()` issues an **implicit `COMMIT`** before executing the script, which
destroys the enclosing savepoint. So `RELEASE SAVEPOINT` at `:374` raises
`no such savepoint: fts_align_empty`, and the `except BaseException` handler's own
`ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT` at `:376` raises the same error — which is the exception that actually
escapes, masking the original.

Verified mechanically in isolation (Python 3.11.15 / SQLite 3.53.1):

```python
c.execute("SAVEPOINT sp")
c.executescript("CREATE TABLE u(y);")   # implicit COMMIT
c.execute("RELEASE SAVEPOINT sp")
# sqlite3.OperationalError: no such savepoint: sp
```

Note the module is already aware of this exact hazard: `hermes_state_schema.py:333-342` defines
`_execute_ddl_script_transactional()` with the docstring *"Execute a DDL script without
`executescript`'s implicit commit."* The savepoint path simply calls the one callee that still uses
raw `executescript`.

## Why it self-heals (and why it's still worth fixing)

Because `executescript` committed, the realignment DDL is **not** rolled back — it persists. The
next open sees `fts_storage_version = 3`, skips the branch, and succeeds. Confirmed on the two
affected profiles: after the one failed open, `fts_storage_version` went `1 → 3` and every
subsequent open was clean.

So: no corruption and no permanent breakage, but the user gets a "session store unavailable" warning
and **loses that one session transcript** (it isn't saved). The savepoint's atomicity guarantee is
also illusory in this branch — a genuine mid-`do_align()` failure would leave partial DDL with the
"rollback" itself erroring out.

## Suggested fix

Either is narrow; maintainers should pick per intent:

1. In `_ensure_fts_schema` (`hermes_state_fts.py:333`), use the existing
   `_execute_ddl_script_transactional(cursor, ddl)` helper instead of `cursor.executescript(ddl)`,
   so no implicit commit occurs and the caller's savepoint stays valid. This keeps the atomicity
   the savepoint was written to provide.
2. Or drop the savepoint in the `not has_messages` branch of `_migrate_misaligned_fts_source`
   (`hermes_state_schema.py:369-379`), since there is nothing to roll back and nothing to index.

A regression test in the style of `tests/hermes_state/test_fts_projection_integrity.py` — open a
misaligned, empty-`messages` DB and assert no exception — would cover it.

## Scope

Reported from a real occurrence on two unused named profiles. Happy to open a PR for option 1 with
the regression test if that's the preferred direction. Reported by @Jpalmer95.

items.title: fix(state): keep the FTS empty-misaligned swap inside the transactional executor

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
## What changed

`_migrate_misaligned_fts_source` has an empty-database fast path (nothing indexed, nothing to index) that swaps the misaligned `messages_fts` shape in place inside `SAVEPOINT fts_align_empty`. The swap reached the DDL through `_ensure_fts_schema`, whose `executescript` issues an implicit `COMMIT` that releases the savepoint mid-swap.

On an empty misaligned database that bypass produced (regression from `42e97f3808`):

```
sqlite3.OperationalError: no such savepoint: fts_align_empty
    cursor.execute("RELEASE SAVEPOINT fts_align_empty")
```

and the recovery `ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT` failed the same way, so the database could not be opened at all.

## Fix

Run the same DDL through `_execute_ddl_script_transactional`, which executes the script statement-by-statement without the implicit commit, so the entire swap stays inside `fts_align_empty` and any failure rolls back the savepoint cleanly before re-raising. This restores the pre-refactor behaviour, which used the transactional call in this spot.

## Tested:

`python -m py_compile hermes_state_schema.py` - OK. `python -m pytest tests/hermes_state/test_fts_projection_integrity.py -q` - 2 passed (closest existing coverage of the misaligned-source migration; no repo test covers the empty branch directly). Scratch probe reopening an empty misaligned DB - pre-fix: `sqlite3.OperationalError: no such savepoint: fts_align_empty`, reopen fails; post-fix: reopen succeeds, `fts_storage_version=3`, `messages_fts` realigned over `messages_fts_src`, search returns the appended row.

items.title: Concurrent InsertAllAsync with FullMutex could leave an orphaned transaction (silent data loss)
items.body:
**Version:** sqlite-net-pcl 1.11.285 (though older versions reproduce this as well since 2018).

## What is the cause of the bug

Two `InsertAllAsync` calls, A and B, on the same pooled connection (FullMutex, so `SkipLock` is set):

1. A: `SaveTransactionPoint` increments `_transactionDepth` 0 → 1 and names its savepoint `S…D0`,
   but has not executed it yet.
2. B: increments `_transactionDepth` 1 → 2, names its savepoint `S…D1` and executes
   `savepoint S…D1` first. SQLite opens the transaction with B's savepoint as the outermost one.
3. A: executes `savepoint S…D0`, which SQLite nests inside B's.
4. A: inserts, then `Release("S…D0")`: the depth check `0 < 2` passes, `_transactionDepth` is set
   to 0 and `release S…D0` runs. SQLite only ends A's nested savepoint; the transaction stays open.
5. B: inserts, then `Release("S…D1")`: the depth check `1 < 0` fails and `DoSavePointExecute`
   throws `ArgumentException: savePoint is not valid` before running any SQL.
   `RunInTransaction` catches it and calls `Rollback()`, which sees `_transactionDepth == 0`
   and does not execute `rollback`.

Result: SQLite is inside a transaction (`sqlite3_get_autocommit == 0`) while sqlite-net's depth
is 0 and the transaction will not be committed. Writes coming after this are on this same transaction, reads are on the
same connection and see the uncommitted rows, so the application behaves normally. And if there are 
`RunInTransaction` calls they nest and release their own savepoints. When the connection ends
without a commit (`Close()`, crash, process killed by the OS), SQLite rolls everything back.
The only trace is the `savePoint is not valid` exception from step 5.

### Code that disables locking when full mutex is enabled
```
// If the database is FullMutex, then we don't need to bother locking
if (ConnectionString.OpenFlags.HasFlag (SQLiteOpenFlags.FullMutex)) {
    Connection.SkipLock = true;
}
```

## Reproducing test
https://github.com/praeclarum/sqlite-net/pull/1314

I ran it in Github codespaces, and got result:
```
Starting test execution, please wait...                                                                          (0.5s)
A total of 1 test files matched the specified pattern.                                                           (1.7s)
  Failed ConcurrentInsertAllAsync [121 ms]
  Error Message:
     Burst 0: write not committed. Errors: [0/3] savePoint is not valid, and should be the result of a call to SaveTransactionPoint. (Parameter 'savePoint'), [0/17] savePoint is not valid, and should be the result of a call to SaveTransactionPoint. (Parameter 'savePoint'), [0/14] no such savepoint: S6197D0, [0/5] savePoint is not valid, and should be the result of a call to SaveTransactionPoint. (Parameter 'savePoint'), [0/10] no such savepoint: S24952D0, [0/7] savePoint is not valid, and should be the result of a call to SaveTransactionPoint. (Parameter 'savePoint')
  Expected: 1
  But was:  0

  Stack Trace:
     at SQLite.Tests.AsyncTests.ConcurrentInsertAllAsync() in /workspaces/sqlite-net/tests/SQLite.Tests/AsyncTests.cs:line 1572
   at NUnit.Framework.Internal.TaskAwaitAdapter.GenericAdapter`1.BlockUntilCompleted()
   at NUnit.Framework.Internal.MessagePumpStrategy.NoMessagePumpStrategy.WaitForCompletion(AwaitAdapter awaitable)
   at NUnit.Framework.Internal.AsyncToSyncAdapter.Await(Func`1 invoke)
   at NUnit.Framework.Internal.Commands.TestMethodCommand.RunTestMethod(TestExecutionContext context)
   at NUnit.Framework.Internal.Commands.TestMethodCommand.Execute(TestExecutionContext context)
   at NUnit.Framework.Internal.Execution.SimpleWorkItem.PerformWork()



Build failed in 22.8s
```

We currently turned FullMutex off, but as it is a default setting I think this might warrant a look from someone that understands this code better than I do.

I also found an issue that is probably related: #1250

items.title: core/vdbe: run full post-commit bookkeeping when COMMIT resumes after I/O
items.body:
A `COMMIT` that yields on IO is finished by re-entering `op_auto_commit`. That re-entry branch returns early, before the post-commit bookkeeping the straight-through path performs at the bottom of the function. Two pieces were missing: `pager.clear_savepoints()` (main plus every attached/temp pager) and `conn.set_cdc_transaction_id(-1)`.

Both are user-visible, in two different ways.

**A savepoint outlives the transaction that owned it.** `COMMIT` destroys every savepoint, so the name must stop resolving. It keeps resolving when the transaction wrote only to an attached database: `SAVEPOINT` always opens a frame on the main pager, but with no main-DB write the main pager never commits a write transaction, so nothing on its own commit path clears that frame — only the skipped `clear_savepoints()` would have. `ROLLBACK TO` and `RELEASE` resolve names against the main pager, so they find the dead frame and return success where SQLite errors.

```sql
ATTACH 'aux.db' AS aux1;
CREATE TABLE aux1.t(x INTEGER PRIMARY KEY);
BEGIN;
SAVEPOINT sp;
INSERT INTO aux1.t VALUES (1);   -- nothing is written to the main database
COMMIT;                          -- yields on IO, resumes through the re-entry branch
ROLLBACK TO sp;                  -- returned OK; must be "no such savepoint: sp"
```

The window is narrow: any write after the COMMIT clears the stale frame through its own commit path, so only the statement immediately following the COMMIT sees it. No data was damaged in this scenario — the symptom is a wrong result, a dead savepoint name that still resolves, not corruption.

**CDC merges two transactions into one.** `conn_txn_id` has get-or-set semantics: the first captured change of a transaction stores the transaction id, and every later change reuses it until the id is reset to `-1` at commit. When the commit yielded on IO the reset never happened, so the *next* transaction's rows were filed under the previous transaction's id — a consumer reading `turso_cdc` sees the second transaction's changes attributed to a transaction that already emitted its COMMIT record.

```sql
BEGIN;
INSERT INTO t VALUES (1);
COMMIT;                     -- yields on IO, resumes through the re-entry branch
INSERT INTO t VALUES (2);   -- autocommit: its own transaction
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT change_txn_id) FROM turso_cdc;  -- returned 1, must be 2
```

The two paths now end in one shared `finish_ended_txn`, so there is no second place to keep in sync.

Deferred foreign-key clearing stays where it was at each site: the re-entry branch clears only after a non-rollback COMMIT, the straight path clears after both. That difference predates this change and is left alone.

## Tests

Two tests in `tests/integration/statement_reset.rs`, one per symptom:

- `commit_resumed_after_io_clears_savepoints` — the attached-database savepoint case above.
- `commit_resumed_after_io_starts_a_new_cdc_transaction` — the CDC transaction-id case above.

Both drive the COMMIT over the existing `QueuedIo` harness, which makes it yield deterministically, and both assert the commit really did yield before checking anything else — so neither can pass by silently missing the re-entry branch.

Red without the fix (`ROLLBACK TO sp` returns Ok; `COUNT(DISTINCT change_txn_id)` is 1), green with it.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Structure and fuzz coverage

Rebased on current main. There are two commits. `2048fafe` adds the tests and the fuzzer change, and they fail on the base. `0bc27e80` adds the fix.

Commit 1 adds a variant of `named_savepoint_differential_fuzz` that runs over `QueuedIo`, where COMMIT yields, with an attached database and explicit BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK. With seeds 1-300 it fails on this bug in 115 runs before the fix and 0 with the fix. It does not open a savepoint outside a transaction yet, because a RELEASE that commits and yields currently loses the savepoint; that is a separate bug with its own fix.

items.title: Leave no open transaction when a transaction helper fails
items.body:
`SQLite.transaction(f, db)` (which `DBInterface.transaction`, `executemany`, and `load!` use) always ran `ROLLBACK TO` + `RELEASE` after an error, and `RELEASE` in `finally`. Two failures follow from that:

1. **Silent data loss after a failed commit.** When the outermost `RELEASE` (the commit) fails with `SQLITE_BUSY`, for example because another connection is still reading, the error is thrown but the transaction stays open. The caller's next statements then run inside it and are rolled back when the connection closes:

   ```julia
   q = DBInterface.execute(reader, "SELECT * FROM t"); first(q)    # another connection mid-read
   SQLite.transaction(() -> DBInterface.execute(db, "INSERT INTO t VALUES (10)"), db)  # throws "database is locked"
   SQLite.intransaction(db)                       # true -- still open
   DBInterface.execute(db, "INSERT INTO t VALUES (20)")  # looks autocommitted
   close(db)                                      # both inserts are gone
   ```

2. **The real error is replaced.** When the failing statement already ended the transaction (`ON CONFLICT ROLLBACK`, `SQLITE_FULL`, ...), the savepoint no longer exists, so `load!(...; on_conflict="ROLLBACK")` reports `no such savepoint: SQLITE5Tc57wbsIv` instead of `UNIQUE constraint failed`.

Changes:
- On failure, roll back only if a transaction is still open; the outermost helper rolls back the whole transaction, so a failed commit no longer leaves it open.
- `load!` finalizes its INSERT statement in a `finally`. Before, a failed `load!` leaked it, and `close(db)` (`sqlite3_close_v2`) then deferred the close, keeping the file and its locks open until GC.
- `ANALYZE` after `load!(...; analyze=true)`, `createindex!`, and `removeduplicates!` now quotes the name like the rest of those functions. A name with a space failed with a syntax error after the rows or index had already been committed. (Separate commit; same lines as `load!`, so kept in this PR to avoid a conflict.)

Verification: two new testsets ("Failed transactions leave no open transaction" fails 5 assertions + 1 error on master; "ANALYZE quotes table and index names" errors on master); full `Pkg.test()` passes locally on Julia 1.12 (SQLite 510/510 plus the other sets).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

items.title: Transaction doesn't rollback, savepoint issue
items.body:
### Issue description

Transaction doesn't rollback when data is in conflict, it doesn't find savepoint or says that no transaction is active

### Expected Behavior

I have the following tables tables : 
Food <-> FoodXStore (join table) <-> Store
Food <-> FoodXTag (join table) <-> Tag
The goal is to create a transaction that does the following : 
0- Begin transaction
1- Insert food 
2- Insert foodXStore joins 
3- Insert foodXTag joins
4- Commit transaction

If any error happens in 1,2 or 3 rollback the transaction like nothing happened to avoid data integrity issues


### Actual Behavior

If the data has no conflict, data inserted correctly.

With data conflict :
Food object is inserted, but on data conflict the joins are not inserted which causes a data integrity issue since the food is inserted with no joins.

Error/Log stack : 
-------------------------------
query:  BEGIN TRANSACTION
query:  INSERT INTO "food"("id", "name",...
query:  SELECT "Food"."...
query:  INSERT INTO "food_x_store"("id", ... -----> FIRST JOIN Inserted successfully
query:  SELECT "FoodXStore"."id" AS ...
query:  INSERT INTO "food_x_store"("id",... -----> SECOND JOIN CAUSING ERROR 
query failed:  INSERT INTO "food_x_store"("id", "foodId", "storeId", "price", "currency") VALUES (NULL, 22, 1, 2, ?) -- PARAMETERS: ["EUR"] ----> ERROR because join already exists and has a unique constraint
Error: Run: RunSQL: run: UNIQUE constraint failed: food_x_store.foodId, food_x_store.storeId
query failed:  ROLLBACK
Error: Query failed: SelectSQL: queryAll: cannot rollback - no transaction is active
-------------------------------

RESULT : 
Food is inserted
FoodStore's first join is inserted
FoodStore's second join is NOT inserted (causing the error)
FoodTags are NOT inserted




### Steps to reproduce

I tried to follow the doc's example using queryRunner : 
https://orkhan.gitbook.io/typeorm/docs/transactions#using-queryrunner-to-create-and-control-state-of-single-database-connection

items.title: feat(assets): back the in-memory database with SQLite's memdb VFS
items.body:
`--database-url sqlite:///:memory:` ran the assets database on [one connection shared by every thread](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI/blob/5c460d8172fe30761ff67c0df3d5643bb74e0d70/app/database/db.py#L240-L263). When the background scan inserted while a prompt registered its outputs, their transactions interleaved on that connection: savepoints vanished under each other (`no such savepoint`), scan batches were dropped and executed outputs went unregistered. This PR puts the in-memory database on SQLite's memdb VFS under a name unique to the process, held open by one connection, so the read and write engines get ordinary pooled connections with normal locking, as they do for a file database. On SQLite older than 3.40.1 or a build without memdb, it logs a warning and keeps the shared-connection behaviour.

**Concurrent scan + prompts + page loads, real process** (Linux, Python 3.12, SQLite 3.53; boot scan of N small input files while 15 prompts each save an image and a client polls `GET /api/assets?limit=100` continuously)

| database | files | runs | runs with errors | `no such savepoint` per run | outputs not registered per run | inputs catalogued | read p95 | read max |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `:memory:` on master | 3,000 | 10 | 10 | 40–58 | 0–10 | 1,367–1,625 | 46–65 ms | 0.31–0.66 s |
| `:memory:` with this PR | 3,000 | 10 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 3,000 | 34–87 ms | 0.37–1.10 s |
| file database | 3,000 | 10 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 3,000 | 39–61 ms | 0.37–0.66 s |
| `:memory:` on master | 10,000 | 3 | 3 | 158–166 | 5–12 | 5,060–5,339 | 43–52 ms | 0.39–0.42 s |
| `:memory:` with this PR | 10,000 | 3 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 10,000 | 33–41 ms | 0.57–0.72 s |
| file database | 10,000 | 3 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 10,000 | 37–41 ms | 0.41–0.47 s |

**The connection held open:** SQLite frees a memdb database when its last connection closes, and the pools close idle connections. Without it, disposing the engines' pools loses every table (`test_database_outlives_its_pooled_connections` fails). Not measured in the real process.

**The 3.40.1 / no-memdb fallback:** before 3.36 opening a memdb name succeeds but every connection gets its own empty database, so the write engine would see no tables. From 3.36 to 3.40.0 the database is shared, but memdb's locking lets a commit rewrite pages under an active read: a real process scanning 3,000 files while running prompts, uploads, tag edits and page loads on SQLite 3.37.2 and 3.39.4 builds failed 40–65 page-load requests per run with `database disk image is malformed` (5 runs), and 0 on 3.40.1 (2 runs); a direct engine probe saw malformed reads in every run on 3.37.2 (12/12), 3.39.x (4/4) and 3.40.0 (5/5), and none on 3.40.1 (0/12). The bundled Pythons are past it: the Windows portable builds' `sqlite3.dll` is 3.49.1 (Python 3.12.10) and 3.50.4 (3.13.14), both with memdb; Python 3.10–3.14 from python-build-standalone ship 3.53. System Pythons linked to an older libsqlite3 (e.g. Ubuntu 22.04's 3.37.2, RHEL 9's 3.34) take the fallback.

Known limitations:
- memdb has no WAL: a write transaction blocks new readers until it ends, and an unfinished read blocks commits. Write transactions are already kept short, which is what keeps page-load reads in the range above.
- memdb caps a database at 1 GiB by default; with minimal metadata a catalogued file takes about 1.2 KB, so roughly 800k files.
